# Project Submission Note

## 1. AI Tools Used
- **Antigravity** (AI coding agent), model: `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Google AI Studio / Gemini API**, model `gemini-3.5-flash`, used by the running system to write follow-up message drafts

## 2. Parts Generated by the Agent
- **Phase 1 (backend):** Express server structure, SQLite setup (`better-sqlite3`), hand-written input validation and
  normalization (`validate.js`), security middleware (Helmet, rate limiting, privacy-safe logger, error handler), the seed
  script, and the automated tests (`tests/patients.test.js`, `tests/security.test.js`).
- **Phase 2 (AI workflow):** `aiService.js`, `draftService.js` and `drafts.js`, the follow-up prompt, the mock fallback,
  atomic approve/reject endpoints, cancelling pending drafts when a patient is completed, the generate rate limit, the
  safety scan test against message-sending code, and the tests (`tests/drafts.test.js`, `tests/ai.test.js`).
- **Documentation:** first drafts of the README and Postman collection.

## 3. Parts I Personally Designed, Decided and Tested
- **Specification and rules:** I wrote the rules given to the agent (stack, response format, safety rules), split the
  work into two phases, and reviewed and approved the agent's plan before each phase was built.
- **Design decisions:** SQLite for easy setup, hand-written validation instead of a library, no CORS and no
  authentication (listed as limitations), and a mock-first AI design so the workflow still runs when the AI is unavailable.
- **Validation rules I set or changed:** strict limits for names, phones, dates and ids; phone numbers must be strings;
  approved draft messages must be 100-500 characters (changed from the original 1-1000, with the mock template checked
  to fit the range).
- **Behavior I changed or added:** the due-today message changes when `includeOverdue` is used; I added the
  `GET /drafts/summary` endpoint with a plain-English summary;
  keeping the cancel-on-complete rule.
- **Testing I did myself:** ran the endpoints manually with Postman, including bad inputs and 409 conflicts, and
  checked that completing a patient cancels their pending drafts.
- **Debugging and AI setup:** configured the Gemini key and model, and investigated why drafts stayed in mock mode
  (`AI_MODE`, `.env` loading, model name, existing drafts) until real AI drafts worked.
- **Git:** created the repository, `.gitignore`, the phase branches and the version tags.

## 4. AI Draft Workflow and Its Limits
- **Real AI mode:** tested with a Gemini API key (`AI_MODE=ai`, model `gemini-3.5-flash`). Drafts generated by the model
  are labeled `"source": "ai"`.
- **Mock mode:** used when `AI_MODE=mock`, the key is missing, or the AI call fails or returns unusable text. It is a
  fixed template with only the first name and visit date filled in, so every mock message reads the same. Drafts are
  labeled `ai` or `mock` so staff always know which they are reviewing.
- **Data sent to the model:** only the patient's first name and follow-up date. Phone numbers and full names are not sent.
- **No automatic sending:** staff must approve every draft, and approval only marks it "ready to send (simulated)". The
  project contains no WhatsApp, SMS or email code.
- **Limits:** AI output varies and can be replaced by the mock if it falls outside the allowed length. There is no
  authentication, so this is not suitable for real patient data.

## 5. How I Used AI Responsibly
The agent wrote most of the code from my rules and plans. I reviewed each plan before it built anything, tested the
endpoints and AI behavior myself, and changed rules the agent's own tests did not question, such as the draft message
length. Every AI-written message goes to a staff member for review before anything could be sent, and the project uses
fictional data only.
